subject.title: trusted-proxy auth: support fallback/default user when identity header is absent

question: Should trusted-proxy auth support an explicit fallback identity when a configured trusted proxy reaches the Gateway without the identity header?
rationale: The choice changes who OpenClaw authenticates as when the upstream proxy provides no per-user identity, affecting Gateway authorization, Control UI access, session scoping, and operator trust boundaries.

options.title: Keep fail-closed and document unsupported
options.body: Reject missing identity headers in trusted-proxy mode and document Cloudflare IP-whitelist/no-identity WebSocket deployments as requiring password auth, Tailscale Serve, or a proxy path that reliably forwards identity.

options.title: Accept narrow opt-in fallback
options.body: Add a named fallback identity only with explicit config, proxy-owned required evidence, allowUsers validation, security audit warnings, and regression coverage.

options.title: Defer to broader auth policy design
options.body: Keep this issue as canonical input while maintainers design a more general identity-bearing proxy policy instead of adding a one-off fallback key.

recommendation.title: Keep fail-closed and document unsupported
recommendation.body: Reject missing identity headers in trusted-proxy mode and document Cloudflare IP-whitelist/no-identity WebSocket deployments as requiring password auth, Tailscale Serve, or a proxy path that reliably forwards identity.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned on the issue and provided the maintainer-side separation from related trusted-proxy fallback work.
